handoff: Changes requested: a like copy that keeps an object value of its target (outcomes, exits…) puts YAML anchors/aliases (&a1/*a1) in the pinned flattened text; all 4 criteria traced to tests, suite green. Minor: a __proto__ step is dropped, not refused.

findings.title: The flattened text of a like copy contains YAML anchors and aliases nobody wrote
findings.detail:
resolveLikes builds the copy with `{ ...of, ...rest }`, so any object value the copy keeps (outcomes, exits, inputs, env…) is the same object as the target's. stringifyYaml (lines 78 and 133) aliases duplicate objects by default, so the pinned and hashed `source` gets `&a1` on the target and `*a1` on the copy. Repro: flattenWorkflowText on a workflow with step `a` (a check with `outcomes: { pass: $done }`) and `b: { like: a }` returns source containing `outcomes: &a1` under `a` and `outcomes: *a1` under `b`. This breaks Plan D2 ('a like copy's keys in its target's order' as the serialization of the flattened document) and D10 ('YAML anchors give way to like:'): the anchors come back in the text people read in a pin, and the fingerprint now depends on object identity rather than on content. The loaded `workflow` value also holds the shared references, so anything that changes one step's object in place would change the other too. The tests miss it because every copy in them replaces its only object-valued key (outcomes).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Pass `aliasDuplicateObjects: false` to both stringifyYaml calls, or deep-copy the target (structuredClone) in resolveLikes. Add a test with a copy that keeps an object key from its target and asserts the source has no `&` or `*` alias.

findings.title: A step named __proto__ is dropped during like resolution instead of refused
findings.detail:
`out[name] = step` with name `__proto__` sets the prototype of `out` instead of adding a key, so the step disappears from the flattened steps. The workflow then loads without it, where a file with the same step but no like is refused by the step-name pattern. Repro: a workflow with `a` (check), `b: { like: a }` and `__proto__: { type: bogus }` flattens to ok:true with only `a` and `b`.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Build `out` with Object.create(null) or as a Map, or use Object.defineProperty, so the step reaches the schema check and is refused.
